headline: High risk of prompt injection and data leakage via shared filesystem/MCP; default writes and broad egress make the pair unsafe without isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files, use MCP, and process stdin/stdout; MemMachine also exposes MCP and conversational context. The pair has a filesystem bridge and a shared tool channel, so attacker-controlled content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. This is not proven by sandboxed evidence, but the documented surfaces make the pathway plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents are connected to the same MCP server or shared workspace
IF MemMachine content is copied into files that Gemini CLI reads as trusted input
mitigations: Disable shared MCP servers between the agents
Separate workspaces so Gemini CLI cannot read MemMachine-managed files
Add a manual review step before Gemini CLI acts on any MemMachine-generated text
Use read-only mounts for any shared directories
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment, and has broad network egress; MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context and can call APIs via MCP. If they share files or prompts, sensitive code or personal context can flow from one agent into the other and then out over networked APIs. The profiles document the surfaces, so the leakage path is credible.
conditions: IF Gemini CLI is pointed at directories containing secrets or private code
IF MemMachine receives those files or summaries through a shared filesystem or MCP bridge
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared directory
Run Gemini CLI in a separate user account or container
Restrict MemMachine to non-sensitive conversational data
Disable outbound API calls for shared test runs
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; MemMachine can also act through MCP and networked APIs. Their overlapping ability to mutate shared resources creates conflict risk if they operate on the same repo or shared backend without locking. The profiles show the overlap, but not any coordination primitive, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or shared directory
IF MemMachine-backed actions and Gemini CLI git operations run concurrently
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working tree
Pause one agent before the other writes shared state
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Limit MemMachine to read-only access during coding sessions
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell commands, and file edits; MemMachine can consume conversational context and act through REST, SDK, or MCP. If MemMachine treats Gemini output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or stored memory. The pairwise pathway is documented by their input/output surfaces, though not directly observed, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MemMachine ingests Gemini CLI output without verification
IF Gemini CLI-generated instructions are used to update long-term memory or trigger API actions
mitigations: Require human approval before MemMachine acts on Gemini output
Add a verification prompt that checks Gemini claims against source files
Keep Gemini output as draft-only text
Log and diff all downstream actions
requires-engineering: implement confidence/provenance gating

E_compliance.rationale: Gemini CLI handles source code, cwd files, and shell environment, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a limited compliance concern is evident: if regulated data is placed into both systems, retention and logging policies may diverge. The other agent is cited because the mismatch is pairwise, not single-agent.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is stored in MemMachine and also processed by Gemini CLI
IF the two systems have different retention or deletion settings
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workflows
Review retention settings for both tools
Document which data classes each agent may store
Use separate projects for regulated and non-regulated work
requires-engineering: align deletion and export handling across systems
